newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Natal University will shed 600 jobs, halve the number of faculties and cut the number of departments by three quarters, its senate said on Thursday.

- Randgold Resources Ltd, the offshore arm of Randgold & Exploration Co Ltd, intends to raise between $120 million and $160 million to fund gold expansion projects when it lists on the London Stock Exchange later this month.

- A late application cost SA Broadcasting Corporation (SABC) television executive Jill Chisholm a place on the short list of candidates to be interviewed for five vacancies on the Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA) council.

- "Alien and invasive" wattle trees in the Eastern Cape are to be turned into high-quality charcoal for export to Europe and the Far East if a local company, Green Charcoal, can put together necessary finance and obtain permission.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Gencor Ltd, the mining house, has struck a $193.6 million dollar deal with Canadian company Eldorado Gold Corp in which Eldorado will acquire two mines in South Africa and exploration sites in Ghana from Gencor, the companies announced on Thursday.

- The National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) on Thursday accused JCI of declaring war after talks between the union and the mining house broke down over JCI's insistence that it could no longer delay cutting about 4,000 jobs.

- Business South Africa (BSA) suggested on Thursday to Tito Mboweni, the labour mininister, that the ill-fated negotiations in Nedlac on the Basic Standards of Employment Bill be postoned until after the presidential jobs summit targeted for October.

- Investigations into the theft of medicines worth hundreds of millions of rands, either from large manufacturers or from the state, have completely disintegrated in KwaZulu-Natal, industry sources said this week.

- The latest agency agreement between the Citrus Board and Outspan, the citrus marketing company, appears to contravene the powers held by the board as it gives Outspan ownership of all fruit delivered to it, industry sources said on Thursday.
SAKE-BEELD
- The National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) wants to obtain a urgent interdict against JCI to prevent the laying off of 4,000 workers at Randfontein Estate Gold Mining Co Ltd at the end of June.
- Hewlett-Packard, one of the world's largest computer groups, is the latest U.S. company to return to South Africa.
THE STAR
- Some robbery-plagued Johannesburg inner-city banks are closing their doors at the weekend after a wave of Saturday armed holdups
- Sunday is D-Day for the South African national soccer side Bafana Bafana if they hope to qualify for their first appearance in the World Cup finals, in France next June.
- Seven years after the Johannesburg Library Gardens underwent a 10.5 million rand revamp, local authorities are considering pulling down structures in the area and starting agian.

- Police have ordered a clampdown on the release of all current crime statistics -- forcing the media and the public to rely on officially audited quarterly reports which will be made public only several months later.
